name: Alpha-lipoic acid
short: Trials: no more adverse events than placebo. Case reports link it to insulin autoimmune syndrome, a rare cause of low blood sugar, in genetically susceptible people.
text: In a meta-analysis of 71 randomised placebo-controlled studies (4749 subjects), alpha-lipoic acid supplementation was not associated with an increased risk of any treatment-emergent adverse event. A European Food Safety Authority panel reviewed 49 case reports of insulin autoimmune syndrome, a rare immune-mediated cause of low blood sugar, that developed after alpha-lipoic acid consumption; all resolved within weeks to months of stopping it. The panel concluded that alpha-lipoic acid in supplements is likely to increase the risk in individuals with certain genetic polymorphisms, who cannot be readily identified without genetic testing, and that the risk cannot be quantified precisely. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
